entries.title: Plugin entry shape

requirements.text: The v2 entry is a module exporting a plugin object with id and setup.
requirements.note: The same object is passed to Plugin.define, so the host receives the recognized fields.

entries.title: ESM package exports break require.resolve

requirements.text: The build resolves the host plugin package through the ESM exports condition instead of a static external list.
requirements.note: Runtime resolve guard keeps host packages external when they resolve.

entries.title: Tool execute return type

requirements.text: Every tool execute result is converted from the v1 shape to the v2 shape.
requirements.note: The bridge runs on both the parsed and the raw execute path.

entries.title: Version double-guard (fail-open)

requirements.text: Setup aborts before registration when the host lacks the session or tool domain.
requirements.note: Fail-closed capability probe before any tool registration.

entries.title: Minimal-surface port for type closures

requirements.text: The role to tool matrix is ported without an i18n or NLP dependency.
requirements.note: The role matrix, its tool groups, and getAllowedToolsForRole live in src/role-matrix.ts, which imports only tool-names.ts. security-policy.ts imports the module and re-exports both symbols for compatibility; the render, generator, agent-add, and guard consumers import the matrix module directly.

entries.title: Arabic code references survive auto-port

requirements.text: Model display names are English-only with no bilingual shape or lang parameter.
requirements.note: One display string per model; no language branch remains.

entries.title: Full-tree port re-writes hand-fixed files

requirements.text: A full-tree port must never overwrite hand-fixed files.
requirements.note: The port tool was deleted at cutover; no port path remains in this tree, so the hazard cannot recur.

entries.title: English-locked translations stub

requirements.text: The translations loader is English-canonical, ships the Arabic table for runtime languages, and has no logger dependency.
requirements.note: The loader resolves keys from the selected dictionary, defaults to English, and falls back to English for an unknown language.

entries.title: Dual-entry v1/v2 adapter (reference: retired)

requirements.text: The entry carries no v1 server member; the v2 host initializes through setup.
requirements.note: 0.1.0 removes the v1 host lane; prove-host-entry asserts the exact entry keys.

entries.title: Conflict-marker debris from stale lint-staged stash applies

requirements.note: The port tool is gone and check:rules rejects every marker class in tracked sources.

requirements.text: The MCP boundary is not applicable because v2 ships no MCP server or client.
requirements.note: No MCP directory, entrypoint, dependency, or live config block exists; the generator ignores a legacy bundle and only the boundary guidance text remains.

requirements.note: prove-s033 binds the seven pieces: quiet resolution, ledger write-behind, the quiet debounce, coordinator jitter, the durable logger stamp, the per-mtime quarantine copy, and the pre-save guard.

requirements.text: Launcher and installer duties stay in the host install script, not in the plugin.
requirements.note: prove-s033 asserts the installer owns candidate discovery, version probing, and scheduling units, and the plugin carries no launcher or installer duty.

requirements.text: The cold-boot launch wave passes only after a recorded cold-boot run meets N1 to N5.
requirements.note: Owner decision 2026-10-30: the cold-boot gate is out of scope for v2. The v1 scorecard keeps the recorded failure (10 of 14 rows overall FAIL, N2 in every one); v2 keeps boot-scorecard-v2.sh but claims no N1-N5 pass. See E-56.

entries.title: v1 retirement transfer — watcher, boot, DB retention, and the unfinished-task census — v2 ACTION REQUIRED before cutover

requirements.text: The watcher policy is owned by the v2 launcher with env over pinned over auto and one decision line.
requirements.note: The rotational probe and the single launcher line are asserted.

requirements.text: DB retention prunes event rows and the backup probe counts both session tables.
requirements.note: The retention and dual-probe behaviour is proven.

requirements.text: The seven-item unchecked-task census is either ported as tests or recorded as out of scope.
requirements.note: Every census item now has its own row (S-053.4 through S-053.10): three are anchored to the v2 code, two are recorded as out of scope, and two are verified by an existing proof.

requirements.text: Pause during a live session halts dispatch and persists the paused handoff set.
requirements.note: prove-s053 pauses two of three handoffs, keeps the original statuses, saves once, refuses a second pause, and restores both statuses on resume.

requirements.text: A task that runs longer than 420 seconds is tracked by the task timeout.
requirements.note: prove-s053 asserts the 420s constant, re-arms one entry, warns once, clears at the bound, and never warns after a clear.

requirements.text: An image-generation 401 refreshes the token once and fails closed on a second 401.
requirements.note: prove-s053 asserts one refresh then success, and a second 401 fails closed with exactly one refresh and no loop.

requirements.text: Confidentiality at rest for plugin state is a host and OS responsibility, not a plugin feature.
requirements.note: State files are HMAC-signed for integrity, not encrypted; the plugin stores no provider credentials, which stay in the host or the OS keyring.

requirements.text: User-level rate limiting is not a single-user local plugin surface.
requirements.note: The plugin classifies provider quotas and defers transient limits to the host; it has no multi-user layer to throttle per user.

requirements.text: Shared state is signed with HMAC-SHA256 before it is written and verified on read.
requirements.note: New writes carry the v2 prefix, both legacy prefixes still verify, and the proof asserts the signature shape and the namespace.

requirements.text: Deleted-agent names persist in the user-owned deletion list and survive a seed.
requirements.note: The generator reads the deletion list and rejects malformed shapes; the seed never writes it and never overwrites an agent file.
